source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: FY2024-25 Integrated Report business review: Lupin's API and CDMO businesses (API Plus, Lupin Manufacturing Solutions Ltd) described as 'reflecting strong alignment with global industry trends such as supply chain diversification, CDMO outsourcing' with ambition to become a 'preferred global API CDMO partner' as customers seek secure, diversified API sources; no explicit revenue figure attributed to China+1 shift.

rural.evidence: India formulations (34% of global sales) includes branded generics/trade generics business (Lupin Life Sciences) and Lupin Diagnostics expanding into Tier 3/Tier 4 towns across 250+ cities; no explicit rural revenue percentage disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Floating vs fixed rate borrowing split not found in accessible sources; third-party analysis (Simply Wall St) notes Lupin holds more cash than total debt and debt-to-equity has fallen from ~34.5% to ~26.3% over 5 years, suggesting low overall leverage/rate sensitivity, but this is not a direct AR disclosure.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company exposed to USD-INR, EUR-INR and ZAR-INR fluctuations across 100+ markets; treasury operations reported to use natural hedges plus forex derivatives in a layered hedging strategy.
inr_exposure.evidence: US FY2025 sales of USD 925 Mn (up from USD 815 Mn in FY2024) represented 36% of Lupin's global sales; risk management disclosures reference natural hedges and forex derivative usage for currency exposure.

pli_scheme.evidence: Lupin (via its API business/Lupin Manufacturing Solutions Ltd, formerly the API Research Park in Pune) is listed as an approved domestic applicant under India's PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals (KSMs/Drug Intermediates/APIs), Group A category; specific incentive amount or revenue contribution not disclosed in accessible sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: IHCL is a domestic hospitality/services company (Taj, Vivanta, Ginger, Gateway brands operating hotels in India and ~12-15 countries); it is not a goods exporter and no China+1/supply-chain diversification narrative appears in company communications.

rural.evidence: No disclosed revenue % from rural markets. Third-party industry coverage describes IHCL's Ginger and Gateway brands expanding into Tier 2/Tier 3 towns and pilgrimage/leisure destinations as a growth engine, with Ginger portfolio reaching 262 hotels and ~68% of operating portfolio in asset-light formats, but no rural revenue contribution figure was found.

govt_capex.evidence: No disclosed revenue % tied to government capex/infrastructure. Contextual/industry-level narrative notes India's push to be a global MICE hub post-G20 (Budget 2025-26 allocated INR 2,541 crore for tourism infrastructure), a demand tailwind for IHCL's MICE/banqueting business, but IHCL-specific quantification was not found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: No floating-vs-fixed debt split found, but IHCL reported a net-cash-positive/near debt-free consolidated balance sheet as of FY2024-25 (gross cash position of INR 3,073 crore), implying low overall rate sensitivity from company borrowings.

crude_exposure.evidence: No disclosed power/fuel/energy cost as % of total expenses was located. IHCL's ESG disclosures note renewable energy sourced ~35-39% of total electricity consumption, which partially mitigates but does not eliminate fuel/energy cost exposure.

inr_exposure.evidence: Directors' Report 'Foreign Exchange Earnings and Outgo' disclosure (year uncertain from available snippets) showed foreign exchange earnings of INR 733.28 crore against outgo of INR 81.65 crore. IHCL earns foreign exchange from international guests and international hotel subsidiaries/management fees, but no current-year USD revenue % or explicit hedging policy could be confirmed.

pli_scheme.evidence: India's PLI scheme covers 14 manufacturing sectors with no hospitality/services category; no indication IHCL participates in or benefits from PLI.

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit China+1 or China-diversification narrative found. Sun Pharma discusses API self-sufficiency (14 API manufacturing sites in India, Hungary, US, Israel, Australia; 400+ APIs) but frames this as vertical integration/self-reliance, not as a China+1 beneficiary story tied to customer diversification away from China.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Not disclosed; company reported a net cash surplus position (~US$3.1bn) at consolidated level, suggesting limited net debt exposure, but no floating-rate liability percentage was found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Not confirmed from a primary-source read; third-party commentary indicates Sun Pharma uses forward contracts and natural hedges (foreign-currency debt/opex) to manage USD/INR and JPY/INR exposure, given large US and emerging-markets revenue base.
inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 non-India (foreign-currency) revenue mix approx.: US 31%, Emerging Markets 18%, RoW 13%, API 4% (~66-67% combined) vs. India Business ~33%, per FY25 results commentary.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sun Pharma was among 55 companies selected under India's ~Rs 15,000 crore PLI scheme for pharmaceuticals covering 41 critical APIs/KSMs/Drug Intermediates; specific incremental-revenue or incentive amount attributable to Sun Pharma was not found in sources reviewed.

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit China+1 or China-diversification narrative found in available third-party summaries; company disclosures emphasize US generics and emerging-markets export growth without a diversification-from-China framing.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company disclosed to use a mix of natural hedges and financial hedging policy (forward contracts) plus a diversified export footprint to moderate INR/USD earnings impact; specific % hedged not confirmed from primary source.
inr_exposure.evidence: North America (US) formulations business contributed approximately 46-51% of consolidated revenue across FY24-25 quarters; India business incl. Consumer Wellness was 39% of consolidated revenue in Q4FY25.

pli_scheme.evidence: No confirmed disclosure found that Zydus Lifesciences is a named beneficiary under the PLI Bulk Drugs or PLI Medical Devices schemes; could not verify via primary annual report due to source access restrictions.

rural.evidence: No explicit rural revenue % disclosed. FY25 commentary notes Regular (mass-market/semi-urban-rural skewed) IMFL volumes returned to growth after 9 quarters of degrowth, while Prestige & Above (more urban/premium) grew to ~41-46% of IMFL volume and ~69-70% of IMFL value in FY25, up from 28.5%/48% in FY19.

crude_exposure.evidence: Company commentary describes grain, ENA (extra neutral alcohol), glass and packaging material costs as volatile/inflationary; gross margins were pressured in FY22-FY24 by grain/ENA inflation and rebounded ~590bps to 42.82% in FY25 as costs eased. Radico commissioned a 350 KLPD grain-based ENA distillery in Sitapur (Sep'23, ~INR 550 cr capex) for raw-material self-sufficiency. No explicit % of raw material cost tied directly to crude oil derivatives found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (largely USD/hard-currency denominated via Gulf duty-free, Africa, APAC and travel retail channels) account for ~5-6% of sales volume and ~9-10% of revenue.

china_plus_one.evidence: USL is an overwhelmingly domestic-focused Indian spirits company (McDowell's No.1, Signature, Royal Challenge, Antiquity). Exports are routed through subsidiary Shaw Wallace Overseas Ltd to ~37 countries but represent a minor, undisclosed share of revenue. No China+1 narrative found.

rural.evidence: MD&A/analyst commentary flags rural and semi-urban demand recovery as a recurring growth theme. Prestige & Above (premium, more urban-skewed) segment was 83% of volumes and ~89% of net sales in FY25, implying Popular/mass segment (more rural/semi-urban weighted) is a minority of net sales. No explicit standalone rural revenue % disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Notes to financial statements: majority of Company's short term and long term borrowings are benchmarked to Bank's MCLR (variable rate), indicating predominant floating-rate debt exposure, though exact percentage of total borrowings was not quantified.

crude_exposure.evidence: CFO commentary: glass bottle costs up 11-17%, paper cartons up nearly 100%, PET resin up 30-50%; 'geopolitical tensions, especially in West Asia, have raised crude oil prices, increasing costs for packaging and energy,' with packaging inflation cutting gross margins by 1.25-1.5pp. Confirms crude-oil-linked packaging/energy input cost exposure, no single raw-material % of revenue figure located.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Central treasury manages FX risk under Board-approved policies covering forex, interest rate and credit risk, using derivative and non-derivative instruments; net FX exposure mainly from export receivables and import payables in USD, EUR, GBP.
inr_exposure.evidence: Revenue overwhelmingly INR-denominated domestic sales; direct USD revenue exposure appears minimal but unquantified.

pli_scheme.evidence: Alcoholic beverages is not among the 14 sectors notified under India's PLI scheme.

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit China+1/supply-chain-diversification-from-China narrative found. AR risk-factor language cites generic 'geopolitical tensions, complexities in the global supply chain... and rising input costs' rather than a China+1 opportunity framing. Ajanta's single API plant (Waluj, Aurangabad) is for captive consumption, not export-diversification-driven.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company widely reported as 'almost debt free'; no specific floating vs fixed rate borrowing breakdown found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Ajanta hedges outstanding export sales via forward contracts; under mark-to-market accounting hedge losses are booked in expenses while gains flow to other income, leaving the company largely protected from net FX impact.
inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (branded generics in Asia/Africa and US generics) contributed ~69% of consolidated revenue in FY2024-25.

pli_scheme.evidence: No confirmed PLI scheme participation found. Ajanta's sole API facility (Waluj) is oriented toward captive/in-house API consumption rather than a PLI-registered bulk-drug/KSM export business.

china_plus_one.evidence: Exports are a minor part of business (~3.9% of sales), largely intra-group shipments to other Nestle affiliates; no China+1 or supply-chain diversification narrative.

rural.evidence: Management described rural India as a significant growth opportunity; rural contribution to sales cited at ~20-25% (up from ~10% in 2016). Company has presence across ~216,000 villages and added ~5.2 lakh outlets across urban/semi-urban/rural markets since April 2023.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Nestle India is a near debt-free company with minimal borrowings; no floating-rate debt percentage disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Cost of materials consumed was ~37.7% of net sales in FY24 (down ~50bps YoY). Company commentary cites crude-oil-linked packaging costs, edible oil/palm oil price volatility, and milk/coffee/cocoa/wheat inflation as key raw-material cost drivers.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Not separately quantified; company sources over 97% of raw materials locally, limiting import/forex cost exposure aside from crude-linked packaging inputs.
inr_exposure.evidence: Company sources more than 97% of materials locally though not fully insulated from crude/edible-oil price moves; export sales (~3.9% of total sales) represent the primary direct USD revenue exposure.

pli_scheme.evidence: On 6 Dec 2021, Nestle India received approval under the PLI Scheme for Food Processing Industry (PLISFPI) for 'processed fruits and vegetables' and 'ready-to-eat/ready-to-cook' categories. No specific incentive amount or revenue attribution disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: International/export business (~45.6% of FY24 consolidated revenue) concentrated in Russia/CIS, South Africa and other emerging markets rather than US/Europe. No explicit China+1 or API supply-chain-diversification narrative found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company reported as 'almost debt free' by FY25 (short-term debt ~INR 138 million as of June 2025); FY23 showed long-term debt ~Rs 251.14 crore and short-term borrowings ~Rs 53.56 crore, but no floating-vs-fixed split found.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company reportedly hedges against currency fluctuations on its export/international book.
inr_exposure.evidence: Secondary source states company 'hedges against currency fluctuations' given ~45.6% international revenue exposure (Russia/CIS, Africa, other emerging markets).

pli_scheme.evidence: No public disclosure found indicating JB Chemicals is an approved participant under API or Bulk Drugs PLI schemes.

china_plus_one.evidence: No mention of China+1, China de-risking, or API sourcing diversification found. Torrent is a branded-generics/formulations player (India, Brazil, Germany, US) with vertically integrated API-to-formulation supply chain, framed as margin/quality control, not China+1.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Average interest rate on borrowings was ~6.26% for year ended 31 March 2024; fixed vs floating rate split not confirmed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Raw material consumption cost was approx Rs 2,776 crore against consolidated revenue of Rs 11,516 crore in FY25 (~24%); inputs are pharma intermediates/APIs/excipients/solvents so crude linkage is indirect at best.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue mix: India ~55%, Brazil ~10% (BRL), US ~10% (USD), Germany ~10% (EUR), Other markets ~15%. Specific hedging policy could not be verified.

pli_scheme.evidence: No confirmed evidence of Torrent Pharma being a named beneficiary under Pharma PLI schemes; primarily a branded-generics/formulations company rather than bulk API/KSM manufacturer.

china_plus_one.evidence: IKS Health is a healthcare BPO/tech-enabled services company delivering services from India-based centers to physician groups, hospitals and healthcare systems in the US, Canada and Australia. No China+1 narrative applicable to this services business model.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Third-party financial data shows consolidated total debt of roughly INR 640 crore (debt-to-equity ~23%); floating-vs-fixed rate borrowings breakdown could not be confirmed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Revenue earned almost entirely from US-based (and Canada/Australia) healthcare provider clients invoiced in USD, while cost base and delivery operations are largely India-based (rupee costs), creating structural USD revenue/INR cost exposure. ~80% of revenue from the US market specifically per DRHP-era summary; precise hedging policy could not be confirmed.

pli_scheme.evidence: IKS Health is a services company, not a manufacturer, so not eligible for PLI schemes which target manufacturing sectors.

china_plus_one.evidence: No China+1 or supply-chain-diversification narrative in the FY25-26 AR. OFSS is a BFSI banking-software vendor (Flexcube, Digital Experience, Banking Platform), not a China-alternative manufacturing/export play. Has a subsidiary Oracle Financial Services Software (Shanghai) Ltd for local market servicing, not a relocation story.

rural.evidence: Not applicable — OFSS sells banking software globally to financial institutions in 160+ countries; no rural-India revenue exposure concept.

govt_capex.evidence: Not applicable/not disclosed — customer base is commercial banks/financial institutions, not Indian government infra spend.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company had zero borrowings (CARO report: no outstanding loans or borrowings due to any lender during the year ended March 31, 2026). OFSS is debt-free; rate-cut sensitivity via floating-rate debt is not applicable.

crude_exposure.evidence: Not applicable — software/IT-services company with no raw-material or crude-oil-linked input costs; cost base is predominantly employee compensation and technology/infrastructure costs.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: OFSS hedges trade receivables in major currencies (USD, EUR, AUD, GBP, JPY) using forward contracts with 30-120 day tenor matched to expected invoice collection; not designated as hedge-accounting relationships, fair-valued through P&L. Net unhedged FX exposure ₹1,443mn as of March 31 2026.
inr_exposure.evidence: Note 24 revenue-by-geography: 91.3% (₹70,042mn of ₹76,721mn FY26 revenue) generated outside India; Americas revenue (largely USD) ~29% of total. The 91.29% figure is a proxy for total foreign-currency revenue exposure rather than USD-exclusive.

pli_scheme.evidence: No mention of PLI scheme anywhere in the AR; India's PLI schemes target manufacturing sectors and do not apply to BFSI software vendors.

china_plus_one.evidence: Analyst/broker coverage consistently frames Divi's as a prime China+1 beneficiary: 'Divi's plays in well as a China+1 strategy for major pharma companies as they look to de-leverage from dependence on Chinese API manufacturers... a perfect alternative to Chinese API giants.' Divi's has backward-integrated into KSMs for Gabapentin, Naproxen, Valsartan and Levetiracetam explicitly 'to reduce import dependency from China.' Custom Synthesis/CRAMS (~45% of sales) targets multinational-innovator diversification demand away from China.

rural.evidence: Not applicable — Divi's is a pure B2B API/CRAMS exporter to global pharma innovators/generics majors, not consumer/rural-facing. Only rural linkage is CSR spend near Visakhapatnam/Hyderabad plants.

govt_capex.evidence: Not applicable — revenue comes from private multinational pharma customers, not government infrastructure spending.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Widely reported as near debt-free with minimal borrowings and very high interest coverage (~1,394x per third-party analysis), implying floating-rate debt exposure is immaterial.

crude_exposure.evidence: Petrochemical-derived solvents and API intermediates cited by broker commentary as a margin driver; 'rise in raw material, power and fuel and shipment costs' pressured FY23 EBITDA, margins compressed to ~32-32.5% from historical 37-40% band. Divi's mitigates via backward integration and >90% solvent recovery.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY2024-25 exports ~90% of consolidated revenue (domestic ~10%), Europe and US together ~74% of sales, implying dominant USD/EUR-denominated revenue and high INR sensitivity.

pli_scheme.evidence: Does not appear on publicly reported approved-beneficiary lists for India's PLI Scheme for Bulk Drugs (initial Feb-2021 cohort or May-2021 waitlist additions). KSM/intermediate backward-integration investments appear self-funded rather than PLI-incentivized.

china_plus_one.evidence: No China+1, supply-chain diversification, or China-related sourcing/export narrative found. Titan is an overwhelmingly domestic consumer business (Tanishq, Titan watches, Eyecare, Taneira) with only a small international retail footprint (UAE, Singapore, newly Atlanta/Santa Clara in the US).

rural.evidence: MD&A/strategy commentary describes a 'Middle India' focused expansion targeting Tier 2/3/4 towns: Tanishq plans B & C town entry with mid-sized stores aiming for ~10% jewellery market share by FY27 via 1,250+ stores across 300+ towns. No explicit rural revenue percentage disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Titan added approximately Rs 3,500 crore to long-term borrowings during FY2024 via NCDs and term loans, but no explicit floating-vs-fixed rate split found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Not applicable — key raw materials are gold, silver and diamonds, not crude oil or petroleum derivatives.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Titan states it remains 'fully hedged at all times' against gold price movements via Gold Metal Loan (GML), gold exchange at outlets (~40-50% of gold procured this way in FY23), and spot buying hedged via forward contracts. ~120-day supply-chain visibility through advance procurement contracts.
inr_exposure.evidence: Gold is imported and priced in USD even though virtually all final sales are domestic (INR), so USD exposure sits primarily on the raw-material/cost side. Revenue-side USD exposure limited to small international Tanishq/Mia retail business (~1% of consolidated revenue, ~Rs 550-561 crore of FY25 consolidated Total Income of Rs 57,818 crore).

pli_scheme.evidence: No mention of PLI scheme participation found. Titan's core segments (jewellery, watches, eyewear, sarees) are not PLI-eligible categories.

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit China+1 framing found. Company shows sustained export momentum (international revenue rose from ~55% of topline in FY25 to 57% in FY26, split India 43%/Europe 26%/Asia Pacific 14%/Middle East & Africa 9%/America 8%) plus active geographic diversification: new UK synthetic slings plant reaching commercial production in Q4 FY25, and a new rigging/distribution facility in Saudi Arabia.

rural.evidence: Not applicable — end markets (mining, infrastructure, oil & gas, elevators, cranes, construction, marine/fisheries) are industrial/B2B, not consumer or rural-facing.

govt_capex.evidence: Management commentary repeatedly cites 'sustained demand in sectors such as oil and gas, mining, and infrastructure' as revenue drivers; Wire Rope segment (72-73% of consolidated revenue) serves mining, infrastructure and construction end-markets heavily influenced by government capex cycles. No explicit numeric % found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Historical AR risk-management disclosures state most long-term borrowings are floating-rate, though current % not retrievable. Company has been rapidly deleveraging: net debt fell to ~Rs 63 crore by end-FY25, reporting a net CASH position of ~Rs 332 crore by end-FY26, sharply reducing rate sensitivity.

crude_exposure.evidence: Steel wire rod is an estimated 90-96% of raw material sourcing (majority from a Tata group steel supplier in Jamshedpur); wire rod/steel is the primary cost input, energy/coking-coal cost-linked rather than crude oil directly. Q3 FY25 raw material costs rose 11.3% YoY.

inr_exposure.evidence: International/export revenue ~57% of consolidated topline in FY26, spread across Europe (26%), Asia Pacific (14%), Middle East & Africa (9%) and America (8%) — meaningful but not purely USD-denominated given UK/Thailand/UAE manufacturing and Saudi/Europe sales presence. Hedge ratios not found.

pli_scheme.evidence: Specialty Steel PLI scheme has selected ~30 companies across multiple rounds (PLI 1.1, 1.2), but no source names Usha Martin among approved beneficiaries/signatories.

china_plus_one.evidence: Glenmark divested 75% of its API subsidiary Glenmark Life Sciences (GLS) to Nirma Ltd (completed FY23-24, retaining ~7.84% residual stake), so the classic China+1 API-sourcing story now sits with GLS/Nirma rather than Glenmark Pharma's own formulations business. Third-party analysis frames China+1 as an industry tailwind, but no direct AR quote attributing revenue growth to China+1 was found.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Finance costs rose ~47.8% YoY in FY24 and total borrowings fell sharply post GLS-Nirma divestiture proceeds (used for deleveraging); no explicit fixed vs floating rate split located.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Company relies primarily on natural hedging for currency exposure rather than extensive forward-contract hedging, per press-reported CFO commentary.
inr_exposure.evidence: North America (largely USD) was ~24.5% of FY2024-25 consolidated revenue (₹32,909 Mn of ₹134,355 Mn); Europe (~21.2%, EUR) and RoW (~20.9%, mixed currencies) add further non-INR exposure, roughly two-thirds of consolidated sales total.

pli_scheme.evidence: Glenmark Pharmaceuticals is listed as one of 9 approved domestic companies in Group A of India's PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals (biopharmaceuticals, complex generics, patented/near-patent-expiry drugs, orphan drugs; ₹11,000 cr of the scheme's ₹15,000 cr outlay earmarked for Group A). No specific incentive income or revenue % disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: No China+1 or China-alternative sourcing framing found. CCL's diversification narrative centers on multi-country green coffee bean sourcing (150+ suppliers across Brazil, Vietnam, India) and Vietnam plant expansion, not on displacing China in any supply chain.

rate_sensitive.evidence: India Ratings affirmed CCL at IND AA-; net leverage ~2.09x FY23, expected to stay elevated ~3.0x over FY24-25 due to Vietnam and India spray-dry capacity expansion (debt-funded). Exact floating vs fixed rate split not found.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw material is green coffee beans (not petroleum-derived), ~1.6kg green beans per 1kg instant coffee. Company operates a cost-plus/presale model shielding margins from raw-material price volatility. Exact raw-material-cost-as-%-of-revenue not found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Chairman Emeritus letter: 'As global supply chains continue to diversify, our strong alignment with India's industrial growth becomes increasingly evident' and 'India is positioning itself as a trusted global hub for clean, scalable production.' Commercial vehicle segment 'impacted by a slowdown in infrastructure activities' tied to elections/government transition.

crude_exposure.evidence: MD&A: 'Material cost accounted for 43% of total income in both FY 2024-25 and FY 2023-24,' primarily special steel alloy bars, iron castings, steel blanks/bolts, alloy steel, aluminium and copper. Commodity price risk is largely a passthrough with time lag; company does not specifically hedge commodities.

inr_exposure.hedging_policy: Board-approved hedging policy primarily using forward contracts to hedge currency risk.
inr_exposure.evidence: 'Large portion of business is transacted in international currencies primarily US$ and EUR... exposed to foreign exchange risk through sales in USA, Europe, China and other countries.' No single consolidated USD-revenue % disclosed; North America alone is 41% of total revenue per segment note (predominantly USD-denominated).

pli_scheme.evidence: Board's Report: 'received certifications for more products i.e. Traction Motor for electric three wheelers, Hub Wheel Integrated Motor for electric two wheelers, under the Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for Automobile and Auto Component Industry.' Chairman's letter: 'We benefited from income accrual from the Auto PLI scheme, for which we had eight products approved.' No specific % of revenue disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: No explicit 'China+1' or API-sourcing diversification narrative for Alkem was found in accessible sources. Broader industry commentary notes India depends on China for ~60-70% of bulk drug/KSM/API imports, but no Alkem-specific statement attributing revenue or order growth to diversification away from China was located.

rural.evidence: Third-party summaries describe Alkem's historical strength in semi-urban/rural and Tier 2-3 town distribution built around its acute-therapy franchise, and note that the Trade Generics (TGx) segment has become a growth driver. No explicit rural revenue percentage was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: US business contributed 19.4% of consolidated revenue in FY25 versus 22.3% in FY24; non-US international/RoW sales contributed 10.5% in FY25 vs 9.9% in FY24.
